title: Finite projective representatives in the specified Tor interval
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $a\le b$ be integers, and let $C\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $C$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $H^i(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $A$-module $N$ and every integer $i<a$ or $b<i$. Here derived tensor is ordinary total tensor after replacing the first factor by a K-flat complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Then there exist a cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of $A$-modules and an isomorphism $Q(P^\bullet)\cong C$ in $D(A)$ such that $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$ and each $P^i$ is a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect), final assertion: representative supported in the given Tor interval.

proof.text: Let $K$ be a K-flat complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] with $Q(K)\cong C$, as in the stipulated computation of derived tensor. The total tensor of $K$ with $A[0]$ is $K$ itself, so $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A$ is represented by $K$ and has the cohomology of $C$. Test the amplitude hypothesis with $N=A$: $H^i(C)=0$ for $i<a$ and for $i>b$.

source.place: Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect), proof of the final assertion

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-bounded-finite-free-model] to the pseudo-coherent object $C$ and its cohomological upper bound $b$. Obtain a complex $F^\bullet$ of finite free modules with $F^i=0$ for $i>b$ and an isomorphism $e:Q(F^\bullet)\cong C$. A finite free module is flat: tensoring with $A^r$ is the finite direct sum of $r$ copies of the identity, which preserves exactness coordinatewise.

source.place: Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect), proof of the final assertion

proof.text: By [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], $F^\bullet$ is K-flat. Its ordinary tensor with a module $N$ computes $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$, whichever K-flat replacement $K$ of $C$ the convention uses: [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], applied to $K$ and to $F^\bullet$ with $L=N[0]$, gives $Q(\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_A N))\cong Q(K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q(N[0])\cong Q(F^\bullet)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q(N[0])\cong Q(\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_A N))$, the middle isomorphism being the derived tensor bifunctor applied to $Q(K)\cong C\cong Q(F^\bullet)$ (the latter is $e^{-1}$). Hence $H^i(F^\bullet\otimes_A N)\cong H^i(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)$ for all $i$, and in particular $H^{a-1}(F^\bullet\otimes_A N)=0$. Apply [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion], with this same integer $a$, to conclude that $M=F^a/\operatorname{im}d_F^{a-1}$ is flat. The exact sequence $F^{a-1}\to F^a\to M\to0$, between finite free modules in the first two positions, is a finite presentation of $M$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect), proof of the final assertion

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective], $M$ is finitely generated and projective. Choose the finite free surjection $A^r\twoheadrightarrow M$ from its presentation. Projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] lifts $\mathrm{id}_M$ through this surjection, giving a section, so $M$ is a direct summand of $A^r$.

source.place: Tag 0658 (lemma-perfect), proof of the final assertion

proof.text: Define $P^i=0$ for $i<a$, $P^a=M$, and $P^i=F^i$ for $i>a$. Its differential out of $M$ is induced by $d_F^a$, which annihilates $\operatorname{im}d_F^{a-1}$; the other differentials are zero or those of $F$. The quotient map $q:F\to P$ is a chain map. For $i<a$, both cohomologies vanish. In degree $a$, $\ker(M\to F^{a+1})=\ker d_F^a/\operatorname{im}d_F^{a-1}=H^a(F)$. For $i>a$, cycles are unchanged and boundaries are unchanged, including $i=a+1$ since $F^a\to M$ is surjective. Hence $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Q(q)$ is invertible [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The isomorphism $e\circ Q(q)^{-1}:Q(P)\cong C$ is the required one. Since $a\le b$, the terms above $b$ are still zero; below $a$ they are zero by construction. The degree-$a$ term is the finite free summand just proved, all higher terms are finite free, and zero terms are summands of $A^0$.
